title: Oral forms: word and emphatic stress

rule.body: Word stress: one syllable in a word is said louder and longer. Most two-syllable nouns and adjectives are stressed on the first syllable (TAble, HAPpy); many two-syllable verbs on the second (beGIN, aGREE). Some words change stress with their job: REcord, PREsent and OBject are nouns; reCORD, preSENT and obJECT are verbs. Emphatic stress: the word said most strongly in a sentence carries the new or contrasting information, so it shows which question the sentence answers.
rule.example: TUNDE bought the car. answers 'Who bought the car?', but Tunde bought the CAR. answers 'What did Tunde buy?'

questions.stem: Which word is stressed on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: table is stressed TA-ble; begin, hotel and agree are stressed on the second syllable.

questions.stem: Which word is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: police is stressed po-LICE; father, garden and water are stressed on the first syllable.

questions.stem: AMAKA cooked the rice. Which question does the sentence answer?
questions.explanation: The stress on AMAKA picks out the person, so it answers 'Who cooked the rice?'

questions.stem: My brother lives in KANO. Which question does the sentence answer?

options.B: Does your brother work in Kano?
options.D: Does your sister live in Kano?

questions.explanation: The stress on KANO gives the place, so it answers 'Where does your brother live?'

questions.stem: In which sentence is the underlined word stressed on the SECOND syllable?

options.C: I keep a [[record]] of my spending.

questions.explanation: As a verb it is re-CORD, as in B; as a noun it is RE-cord, as in A, C and D.

questions.stem: Which of these words is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: important is stressed im-POR-tant; beautiful, yesterday and family are stressed on the first syllable.

questions.stem: In which sentence is the underlined word stressed on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: The noun present is PRE-sent, as in C; the verbs in A, B and D are stressed ob-JECT, pre-SENT and ex-PORTS.

questions.stem: Bola ate TWO oranges yesterday. Which question does the sentence answer?

options.A: How many oranges did Bola eat yesterday?
options.B: When did Bola eat two oranges?

questions.explanation: The stress on TWO gives the number, so it answers 'How many oranges did Bola eat yesterday?'

questions.stem: Which word is stressed on the THIRD syllable?
questions.explanation: understand is stressed un-der-STAND; pho-TOG-ra-phy is 2nd, ex-am-i-NA-tion 4th, COM-for-ta-ble 1st.

questions.stem: Ngozi gave the book to her TEACHER. Which question does the sentence answer?

options.A: Did Ngozi give the pen to her teacher?
options.B: Did Ngozi give the book to her friend?
options.C: Did Ada give the book to her teacher?
options.D: Did Ngozi lend the book to her teacher?

questions.explanation: The stress on TEACHER corrects the person who got the book, so it answers 'Did Ngozi give the book to her friend?'
